auth.title: Authentication
auth.snippet:
The API authenticates using access tokens (API keys). You can [generate access tokens](https://help.smartsheet.com/articles/2482389-generate-API-key) in the Smartsheet UI.
> **Important:** Smartsheet Gov and Smartsheet Regions Europe use separate tokens from Smartsheet.com.
Each API request requires passing in an access token as the `Bearer` value in your authorization header. For example,
`Authorization: Bearer JKlMNOpQ12RStUVwxYZAbcde3F5g6hijklM789`
This article provides best practices to consider when working with the Smartsheet API and any access tokens (API keys), or other sensitive information.
## Authentication Approaches
When choosing an authentication method, it is important to consider your integration scenario. Is the integration machine-to-machine without user interaction, or do you want user consent and interaction?
- **If your scenario involves user consent and interaction,** it's typically best to use OAuth with Smartsheet. Note that the Smartsheet implementation of OAuth 2.0 is a 3-legged process, which requires human intervention. See [OAuth Walkthrough](https://developers.smartsheet.com/api/smartsheet/guides/advanced-topics/oauth) for details.
- **If your scenario is strictly machine-to-machine,** execute raw token requests over HTTPS. It's a straightforward, secure way to authenticate. See [Access Token Best Practices](https://developers.smartsheet.com/api/smartsheet/guides/basics/authentication#access-token-best-practices) for details.
Each scenario requires an HTTP authorization header containing an access token.
> **Note**: In applications and for routine requests, it is best to use a shared account, such as ticket-processor@example.com, rather than your individual work account.
> **Warning**: If an unauthorized user gets a copy of this token, they will be able to access all Smartsheet data that you have access to, both to read and modify on your behalf. You should keep your tokens secure and do not share them with anyone.
## Access Token Best Practices
You can [generate access tokens](https://help.smartsheet.com/articles/2482389-generate-API-key) in the Smartsheet UI.
Never commit access tokens (API keys) to accessible version control systems like GitHub or BitBucket. Instead, use one of the following recommended storage options.
- Use an app configuration tool suitable for deploying secrets to your app, or
- Use a config file outside of source control, or
- Use environment variables set outside of source control.

auth.snippet:
OAuth 2.0 (OAuth) provides a way for your app users to grant limited access to their Smartsheet resources. Here, we demonstrate registering apps to use OAuth and implementing an OAuth flow with your apps.
> **Note:** The Smartsheet [SDKs](https://developers.smartsheet.com/api/smartsheet/guides/additional-resources#sdks-and-samples) also support OAuth 2.0.
## Register for Developer Tools
Developer Tools is a Smartsheet user interface for registering client applications that use OAuth to access Smartsheet user resources with the user's consent. Here's how to register for Developer Tools.
1. Designate a Smartsheet account for using OAuth with your apps.
> **Tip:** A best practice is to use an additional Smartsheet account (a *service account*) that you don't personally use in the Smartsheet application.
2. Go to the [Developer Tools Registration](https://developers.smartsheet.com/register) page.
![](https://developers.smartsheet.com/assets/oauth-developer-tools-registration.948476e409c5b4304d8da2ce6a91815644c4fb24017a2d66d7e2ba5b68bc2c43.5ffd95b9.png)
3. In the Developer Tools Registration page, enter the email address of a user account to associate with your apps.
4. Read the [Smartsheet Developer Agreement](https://www.smartsheet.com/legal/developer-program-agreement). If you agree and are ready to register your user, click **Register User Account**.
A developer tools registration confirmation message appears.
Upon accepting your request, Smartsheet activates the Developer Tools user interface for the user account.
> **Note:** If Smartsheet denies your request, consult with your Customer Success Manager.

4. Save your profile.

auth.title: Get Started
auth.snippet:
Making your first API call is as easy as **generating an API access token** and **sending a request** to one of our API endpoints.

## Generate an API access token
**Required plan:** Business, Enterprise, or Advanced Work Management
Generate an API access token in the Smartsheet UI.
1. Go to the Smartsheet UI.
2. Select your **Account** icon in the lower-left corner of the screen, and then select **Personal Settings**. The Personal Settings page for your account appears.
3. Select the **API Access** tab.
4. Click the **Generate new access token** button to generate an API access token.
![](/assets/generate-api-token.88baa369e3a9a493b9b77c98f575bdedf4f5122f5a96b85e4414f44817635503.99ff9e22.png)
5. Note your access token and store it in a secure location. See [Access Token Best Practices](/api/smartsheet/guides/basics/authentication#access-token-best-practices).
> **Note:** Tokens generated for Smartsheet, Smartsheet Regions instances, and Smartsheet Gov use the above generation process.
>
> However, these tokens aren't interchangeable.
>
> - A token generated on Smartsheet doesn't work on a Smartsheet Regions instance or Smartsheet Gov.
> - Each environment requires a token specifically generated for it.
## Call an API endpoint operation
You can call an operation right from within this documentation site.
1. Navigate to the page of an operation you want to call.
For example, go to the [List workspaces](/api/smartsheet/openapi/workspaces/list-workspaces) page.
2. Click the **Try it** button, under the example request code on the right side of the operation page.
![](/assets/click-try-it.7db98ecfeea1473f1ba07e3482075ef232d740da0affdff083e345e1d2a18c18.99ff9e22.png)
A request editor appears.
![](/assets/query-editor.534fb020a08f94551ded9eabd462added6e91c5355f74c4ac596233537d8930b.99ff9e22.png)
3. Apply your API access token in the **Security** tab by selecting the **Bearer Token** value field and then selecting **Set value** to start replacing the current value.
![](/assets/api-token-set-value.539eb9d3877753414c7218b19f4d6852bfa524e6befc9d2f4f6287e0e648c38b.99ff9e22.png)
4. In the **Query** tab, set or unset the operation's query parameters.
![](/assets/query-tab.234203a8f245879cee2d9701387d47191de46921ad2130d9dd8c4a03ff0c87cc.99ff9e22.png)
5. When you're ready to call the operation, click the **Send** button. A response appears in the **Response** tab, at the bottom left of the editor window.
![](/assets/response.30a328f88cd23b4c5be6a9bdab845c85d7799be89f98db

access.title: API FAQ | Smartsheet Developers
access.snippet:
**Is there a fee to use the API?**
No. The use of the API is free to all Smartsheet customers, regardless of plan, and third party application developers.
**How do I access the API?**
If you are a Smartsheet customer, you can use the API to directly access your data and integrate your Smartsheet account with other systems or applications. Simply go to your Personal Settings > API Access to generate an access token. Our detailed[ documentation](http://smartsheet.com/developers/api-documentation) will guide you through a variety of scenarios, from retrieving and updating your sheet contents to managing your users and executing org-wide data backups.
If you are an application developer, we are committed to making it easy to build on top of Smartsheet - whether you are developing a solution for your organization or creating an app for the Smartsheet customer community at large. Use standard OAuth2 authentication and authorization to safely access Smartsheet data on behalf of your users without requesting or storing their usernames or passwords. Take advantage of granular access scopes to request only the level of access required for your app. To get the ball rolling,[ sign up](http://smartsheet.com/developers/register) for a Smartsheet developer account, register your app to get app key and secret and follow our[ docs](http://smartsheet.com/developers/api-documentation) to create your first Smartsheet app.

mcp.title: Install the Smartsheet MCP server
mcp.snippet:
# Install the Smartsheet MCP server
You can connect various AI assistants to the Smartsheet Model Context Protocol (MCP) server. Connected to the Smartsheet MCP server, you can interact with your Smartsheet data using natural language.
**Required plan:** Business, Enterprise, or Advanced Work Management

Here's what a Smartsheet MCP server connection requires:
- Network access to a Smartsheet production server environment
- Valid Smartsheet API token, unless you're connecting an AI tool that supports Smartsheet's OAuth, such as ChatGPT (web or mobile), Claude AI, Claude Desktop, Gemini Enterprise Plus, or Microsoft 365 Copilot.
To create an API token, refer to the [Get started](https://developers.smartsheet.com/api/smartsheet/guides/getting-started#generate-an-api-access-token) article.
- URL for the MCP server production environment in your target region. Refer to the table below.
**Region URLs**
| **Region** | **Environment** | **MCP server URL** |
|---|---|---|
| United States | US production | `https://mcp.smartsheet.com` |
| Europe | EU production | `https://mcp.smartsheet.eu` |
| Australia | AU production | `https://mcp.smartsheet.au` |

mcp.title: Workflow context for AI agents with Smartsheet MCP on AWS | Amazon Web Services
mcp.snippet:
[Smartsheet](https://www.smartsheet.com/) has launched a generally available Model Context Protocol (MCP) Server.
With [the Smartsheet MCP Server](https://developers.smartsheet.com/ai-mcp/smartsheet/mcp-server), AI assistants can read, write, and manage Smartsheet data through a standardized protocol. The protocol spans more than 40 tools for exploring, creating, and managing sheets, rows, columns, and automations. You can update task statuses, create rows, and modify project structure directly through natural language.

[Kiro](https://kiro.dev/) is an agentic IDE where developers connect to Smartsheet through MCP to reference project specs, update task status, and track dependencies without leaving their coding workflow.

Smartsheet MCP Server delivers precisely structured context, including row relationships, column types, cell history, and comments. This produces token-efficient payload sizes rather than returning raw API payloads. This engineering decision compounds into reduced cost and improved latency at scale when running hundreds of AI-assisted queries across a project portfolio.

The Smartsheet MCP Server is available at three regional endpoints. It uses Streamable HTTP transport (MCP spec versions 2025-06-18 and 2025-03-26) and is authenticated with either OAuth 2.0 or a Personal Access Token.
- Commercial US: https://mcp.smartsheet.com.
- EU: https://mcp.smartsheet.eu.
- AU: https://mcp.smartsheet.au.

[Kiro](https://kiro.dev/docs/mcp/) is the right path when developers want Smartsheet project context available directly in their development environment, alongside their code, without context-switching.
Kiro is built around spec-driven development. It turns high-level prompts into structured specs, then into working code, docs, and tests. MCP servers are how Kiro gets real-world context by connecting to documentation, databases, APIs, and enterprise systems to ground its agent in live data rather than training-time knowledge.
A Kiro feature called powers is a one-click installable bundle that packages a curated MCP server with steering files and hooks. It gives the Kiro coding agent a new capability out of the box. For Smartsheet, configuring the connection takes a single JSON configuration block and from that point, the Kiro agent can reference live project data as part of a development workflow.

mcp.title: Smartsheet MCP server tools
mcp.snippet:
The Smartsheet Model Context Protocol (MCP) server provides a way to leverage Smartsheet’s public API via AI clients, allowing you to interact with your data using natural language. The MCP server's underlying **tools** (operations) interact with your Smartsheet data (with your permission) to respond to your prompts. The following sections describe the key tools available to your AI client once [connected](https://developers.smartsheet.com/ai-mcp/smartsheet/install-the-smartsheet-mcp-server) to the Smartsheet MCP server.
**Required plan:** Business, Enterprise, or Advanced Work Management
To execute any tool, your AI client requires specific OAuth access scopes. Each tool lists its Access scopes below its name.
For starters, explore the discovery and navigation tools.
*Tokens* are the basic units that AI language models use to process text. They're chunks of text that can be individual words, parts of words, or even punctuation marks. Both your input and the AI's responses are measured in tokens. This matters because:
- Models have maximum token limits (context windows)
- Processing speed decreases with increasing token count

**Key Features**
- **Fuzzy Matching**: Supports approximate matching, so you don't need exact names.
- **Results Context**: Returns asset names, types, parent folder/workspace context, match excerpts, and favorite indicators.
- **Maximum Results**: Returns up to 100 results (no pagination available).
- **Wide Coverage**: Can search across sheets, reports, dashboards, folders, workspaces, and more in one call.

mcp.title: Smartsheet MCP server introduction
mcp.snippet:
Interact with your project data in Smartsheet using the Smartsheet MCP server connected to Claude, ChatGPT, and other AI clients. Once connected, you can use natural language to read, analyze, and manage Smartsheet data to complement how you make decisions and get work done.

Our [Quickstart](https://developers.smartsheet.com/ai-mcp/smartsheet/mcp-quickstart) walks you through connecting the Smartsheet MCP server as an interactive companion in Claude Code. (These connection principles work across MCP-compatible AI clients.)
## Why use the MCP server?
The Smartsheet MCP server bridges the gap between Smartsheet and AI models, allowing you to:
- Access Smartsheet data in real time
- Apply AI reasoning with Smartsheet's project and data management features
- Integrate with popular AI platforms including ChatGPT, Claude, Cursor, Microsoft 365 Copilot, and Gemini Enterprise Plus, or custom AI clients.
- Automate complex tasks that require both data analysis and decision-making
Instead of manually copying data into an AI or writing custom API integrations, you can connect Smartsheet to AI clients to query projects, transform data, and trigger actions.
## How it works
The MCP server exposes Smartsheet capabilities as tools that AI models can invoke. When you integrate Smartsheet with an AI client:
1. The AI client can access (with your consent) predefined tools to summarize sheets, create rows, update data, and more.
2. The client determines which tools are needed to solve your requests.
3. The MCP server executes the request and returns structured data.
4. The AI client processes the results and provides a response.
This enables natural interactions like: *"Show me all overdue tasks from the Marketing sheet and create a summary report"* or *"Update all project statuses based on the latest timeline changes."*

mcp.title: Quickstart with the MCP server
mcp.snippet:
Here you'll connect to Claude Code and use the MCP server as your coding companion to explore sheet structure, understand your data, and prepare for writing API code. (These connection principles work across MCP-compatible AI clients.)

```
export SMARTSHEET_API_TOKEN="token value"
```

## Step 2: Configure your MCP server connection
Use Claude Code's CLI, to configure your connection.
```
claude mcp add --transport http smartsheet-mcp \
https://mcp.smartsheet.com \
-H "Authorization:Bearer ${SMARTSHEET_API_TOKEN}"
```
If you're using a regional server outside of the US, replace the MCP server URL with one for your region:
- For Europe, use `https://mcp.smartsheet.eu`
- For Australia, use `https://mcp.smartsheet.au`
